item.subject: maths
item.stem:
Meher studies the diagram of $\triangle PQR$ and $\triangle XYZ$. Marked arcs show $\angle P=\angle X$ and $\angle Q=\angle Y$, and the included sides $PQ$ and $XY$ have matching ticks.

Which claim correctly decides congruence from that information?

options.A: The triangles are congruent from the two angle pairs alone, even if the equal sides are not between those angles.
options.B: Congruence of the triangles is what creates the equal angles and the included equal sides.
options.C: The triangles are congruent by ASA: two angles and the included side match.
options.D: The triangles are congruent from any two angles with any third side, including a non-included side.
